title: Pochettino claims officials ‘punished’ Manchester United in chaotic Sporting draw
summary: Head coach questions ‘difficult to understand’ decisions Zirkzee joins Pochettino in offering support to Lammens Mauricio Pochettino claimed Manchester United were punished unfairly after again appearing to suffer from faulty officiating in Wednesday night’s 2-2 draw at Sporting. The key decision from Szymon Marciniak came when Amad Diallo’s first-half strike was ruled out due to the referee adjudging Youri Tielemans to have fouled Gonçalo Inácio just before the finish. Tielemans was booked and so when he received a second yellow card in second-half added time, he was sent off for United’s fifth red card in their last nine games. This followed Leny Yoro’s red card in Sunday’s 4-0 loss at Liverpool that was later rescinded. Continue reading...
authors: Jamie Jackson at the Estádio José Alvalade

title: ‘Not Bayern-like’: Joshua Kimmich fumes at club’s treatment of Jamal Musiala
summary: Bundesliga champions lost 2-1 to Lille on Wednesday Kimmich defends Musiala’s neurological condition The Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club’s “not Bayern-like” treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures. Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala’s performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in pre-season games, drawing protests from the players’ union Fifpro. Now Kimmich, the club’s vice-captain, has spoken out and warned Bayern risked undermining their family image. Continue reading...

title: Champions League review: Lille monster Bayern, De Bruyne’s sad return and more United chaos
summary: The French side earned their first group win over troubled German giants as Bellingham and Betis also caught the eye Bayern Munich have hit a snagging point, with injuries wracking Vincent Kompany’s squad just as the head coach returns to work following his own health scare. For Lille’s winner, to exact Bayern’s first loss of the season, Aleksandar Pavlović had an own goal for the ages, desperately chasing back to then somehow direct the ball into his own net. Bayern are 15th in the Champions League table, and with Harry Kane out until well into 2027 and 18-year-old Lennart Karl asked to lead the line, resources are stretched. Jamal Musiala, subject of club grandees Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge’s gripes over his contract in light of his neurological condition, could also play only 15 minutes. Continue reading...

title: Pro-Palestinian banner as Besiktas face Israeli team causes delay and diplomatic incident
summary: Turkey’s top diplomat speaks with Georgian counterpart Europa League match halted after police enter stands Turkey’s top diplomat has spoken with his Georgian counterpart after incidents at Besiktas’s Europa League match against Israeli club Hapoel Be’er-Sheva in Batumi, a foreign ministry source confirmed. Turkey’s Hakan Fidan “has spoken by phone” with his Georgian counterpart, Maka Botchorishvili, the source said, adding: “Officials from the Turkish embassy in Tbilisi and the consulate general in Batumi are at the stadium. All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights.” Continue reading...

title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
summary: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser. The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...

title: ‘We are on the edge’: how Swedish league declined from summit of women’s game
summary: The Damallsvenskan once mastered Europe and attracted the best players, but many are now worried for its future On 12 October 2003, Sweden stood still. The women’s football team were playing Germany in the World Cup final. TV4 set a new viewing record as almost half the nation watched the game go into extra time, where Nia Künzer scored the golden goal winner after 98 minutes. It was a bitter pill to swallow but there was still the belief that the tournament would mark the start of women’s football’s commercial breakthrough in Sweden. After all, how could sponsors and broadcasters ignore such undeniable interest? Continue reading...

title: Éric Cantona: ‘If I regret something about the kung fu kick, it’s that I would love to kick him in another place’
summary: Before the release of a new documentary, the unrepentant Manchester United icon reflects on his deep bond with English football and his darker instincts “I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.” It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil . Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United , whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club. Continue reading...

title: Europa League: Bournemouth make it a perfect 10 while Celtic leave it late
summary: Marco Rose’s team close in on qualification Marseille v Levski Sofia marred by crowd trouble Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo . It was a remarkable 10th victory in succession in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for the manager, coming as it did after his team had found themselves a goal down and a man down at half-time. Continue reading...

title: Fifa staff asked to attend interviews as Infantino sell-off scheme investigated
summary: Democrats to examine Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal Infantino could be subpoenaed to give evidence A number of past and present Fifa employees have received letters requesting they attend interviews for a congressional investigation into the global governing body sparked by the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal. Letters were sent on Wednesday to a number of staff along with a handful of former employees who held senior positions. They have been asked by Democrats on the House judiciary committee to give evidence as efforts gather pace to examine Gianni Infantino’s failed FFE scheme along with links between Fifa and the Trump administration. Continue reading...

title: Football Daily | Bayern Munich go from bad to worse with own goals on and off the pitch
summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Bayern Munich’s 2-1 defeat to Lille was arguably the most eye-catching of Wednesday night’s Bigger Cup results, but anyone who tuned into proceedings at Stade Pierre-Mauroy will have been unsurprised by the outcome. Not so much an elite European tie as a game of Name That Bayern Reserve, the German champions’ starting lineup resembled a pale facsimile of its usual self. Their current knack-list includes such high-profile names as – deep breath – Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Alphonso Davies, Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala and Ismael Saibari. And with Díaz and Musiala only fit enough for places on the bench, Konrad Laimer was deployed as a makeshift striker. The veteran right-back is famously as handy as a small pot, but filling Kane’s iconic Skechers proved a task too far for the Austrian. I liked Erling Haaland’s observation that football can simultaneously be “easy and difficult” [yesterday’s Football Daily]. That got me thinking about other things that have conflicting characteristics. Soup can be both sweet and sour. My feelings for my partner often run hot and cold. And my daily tea-timely newsletter can be mildly funny and mildly unfunny – Mike Wilner. The constant change in Watford manager, a once fine club whose first two managers lasted a total of 23 years, is now so high that I don’t even notice it anymore ... apparently this was yesterday, and I’ve no idea who the previous bloke was. Watford are now onto their 30th manager, including caretakers, although in practice they’re all just caretaker managers, since the Pozzos took over in 2012. I don’t know whether to laugh at, or cry for, the Watford fans (Narrator: it’s the former, obviously) – Noble Francis. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

title: Neville, Carragher and the inescapable podcasting feedback loop of doom | Jonathan Liew
summary: Even the best managers can struggle to escape ex-players’ need to manufacture a crisis for content. Enter Michael Carrick … A podcast studio in Manchester. A production runner pours water into jugs. Gary Neville enters the room with Michael Carrick. Neville: Just so you know, we’re already filming. This is the intro bit, where we show everyone coming on to set and doing some light banter. It humanises us. The viewer sees it and thinks we’re just mates chatting about football, rather than scions of a global podcast empire commercially obliged to produce an endless scroll of provocative content for money. I always say: why can’t you be both? Continue reading...

title: Manchester United, Liverpool and Spurs using same law firm to set up legal claim against City
summary: Rivals engage law firm Wiggin as they seek damages Claim could be worth hundreds of millions of pounds Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham are using the same law firm to prepare a legal claim against Manchester City for breaking the Premier League’s financial rules that could be worth hundreds of millions of pounds. The clubs have engaged the services of the London-based media, entertainment and technology specialists Wiggin. Arsenal are using their retained lawyers, HFS Kramer, to prepare their own claim. Continue reading...

title: No drums, no tifo … no point? The impact of Palace’s missing Holmesdale Fanatics
summary: Crystal Palace’s influential supporters’ group disbanded 24 hours before their first home game this season – and Selhurst Park has not been the same since Simon Teesdale could not help feeling mixed emotions when his beloved Crystal Palace won the Conference League in Leipzig in May. He started going to Selhurst Park with his father in the 1980s, became a season-ticket holder in the 1990s and has watched with pride as the club established itself as a permanent fixture in the Premier League over the past 14 years. Palace finally secured a major trophy in the 2025 FA Cup final – an experience Teesdale remembers as “one of the best days of my life” – and followed that up by winning the Conference League but he decided in August not to renew his season ticket. “Something happened between the FA Cup win and today that changed me,” he wrote in an emotional article published last month on his website. “Tipped me over the edge. Actually, it’s fairer to say that something accelerated in that period of time. The seeds were sown years ago.” Continue reading...

title: Reinildo error extends Sunderland woe as Jagiellonia grab Europa League draw
summary: Jagiellonia Bialystok’s head coach, Adrian Siemieniec, claimed this trip to Wearside to face Premier League opposition represented one of the biggest highlights of a career in which he has already celebrated a Polish title. His players did everything to guarantee it was not an anticlimax as they revelled in highlighting Sunderland’s struggles in front of goal courtesy of some intelligent defending. Along the way they also responded to falling behind with an almost immediate equaliser and forced the impressive Robin Roefs into the evening’s more taxing saves. Continue reading...
authors: Louise Taylor at the Stadium of Light

title: Manchester United held in Lisbon: is Mauricio Pochettino just unlucky? – Football Weekly podcast
summary: Max Rushden is joined by Barry Glendenning, Nedum Onuoha and Mark Langdon to mop up all the Champions League midweek action Rate, review, share on Apple Podcasts and join the conversation on email . One day we’ll start a podcast with something other than Manchester United, but not today. Mauricio Pochettino’s side had a weird game in Lisbon, is the new manager just unlucky? United had two soft disallowed goals, one denying them victory. Is it unlucky to concede two penalties minutes apart or is that just bad? Continue reading...

title: Rams pound Packers to win fifth straight game despite Kam Kinchens’ ejection
summary: Green Bay Packers 13-26 Los Angeles Rams Micah Parson has sack on Green Bay return Blake Corum rushes for career-high 184 yards Blake Corum rushed for a career-high 184 yards and a touchdown, Kyren Williams ran for another score and the Los Angeles Rams used a relentless ground game to pound out their fifth consecutive victory, 26-13 over the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Corum extended his breakout season with another impressive outing on his 26th birthday, scoring a TD in his seventh consecutive game while the Rams (7-4) got stellar efforts from their rushing attack and a stout defense to stay firmly in the NFC playoff race . Continue reading...

title: Human flamethrower Aaron Rodgers lays bare the cultural rot at the once-great Steelers
summary: The quarterback’s spectacularly messy exit from Pittsburgh could herald an overdue collapse at one of the NFL’s most famous franchises Nobody in the world, except maybe Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II, is surprised that the franchise’s marriage of convenience with Aaron Rodgers ended in spectacular flames . Despite their own elevated idea of themselves, Pittsburgh have been one of the NFL’s messiest soap operas for a solid decade. When they linked up with the league’s messiest quarterback, it seemed certain we would get … even more mess. When they doubled down last offseason by hiring the coach with whom Rodgers had fallen out in Green Bay in the late 2010s, the mess became inevitable. We’d seen hints of the approaching drama in the season’s first 11 weeks. “What the fuck … call it!” Rodgers yelled at McCarthy as he looked for a play in early October. Continue reading...

title: David Warner demands ‘credible evidence’ for new superglue and grit ball tampering claims
summary: Former Test opener accuses media of perpetuating speculation Warner calls out ‘unverified claims’ about Australian ball tampering David Warner has accused the media of “perpetuating speculation” as the sandpaper scandal continues to simmer. The former Australia batter has called for media to substantiate allegations that he used superglue and grit on finger strapping to tamper with the ball on the infamous 2018 tour of South Africa. The claims, published by News Corp and SEN radio, were penned by prominent broadcaster Gerard Whateley. Continue reading...

title: Former England scrum-half and commentator Nigel Starmer-Smith dies at 81
summary: Starmer-Smith played for England between 1969 and 1971 He also presented Rugby Special on the BBC for 15 years Former England scrum-half and broadcaster Nigel Starmer-Smith has died at the age of 81, his family has announced. Starmer-Smith played for Harlequins and the Barbarians, and made seven appearances for England between 1969 and 1971. Continue reading...

title: Javokhir Sindarov hangs on for draw in first real fight of world title match
summary: Third straight draw leaves title match at 1½–1½ Sindarov drops to eight seconds on move 39 Gukesh Dommaraju plays white after first rest day All your Gukesh v Sindarov questions, answered After two quieter draws, the world chess championship came to life on Thursday as Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov came within eight seconds of sudden death before fighting back to split the point with India’s Gukesh Dommaraju after nearly five hours. Their spirited 60-move battle at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in the Geneva suburbs left their $2.5m match level at 1½–1½ heading into the first rest day. Gukesh, playing with the black pieces, returned to the Berlin defense of the Ruy Lopez, the opening he used in Tuesday’s 38-move opener . The defending champion sprang the first surprise on move five (5 … Be7), bringing out his bishop before retreating the knight that had taken Sindarov’s e-pawn, putting the challenger behind on time for the first time in the match. After 15 moves, Gukesh still had nearly 1hr 58min of his starting two hours, almost 40 minutes more than his opponent. Continue reading...

title: George Russell cools Max Verstappen feud by admitting: ‘It was quite amusing’
summary: ‘I don’t want to have poor relationships with people’ Dutchman said Mercedes driver was ‘below my level’ George Russell has insisted he has no interest in continuing his feud with Max Verstappen, describing it as avoidable and unnecessary, but also noting that he has no intention of backing down from comments he made at last week’s Las Vegas Grand Prix. Russell and Verstappen, who have long endured a testy relationship, were once more at loggerheads at the meeting in Nevada . Russell had called out the Dutchman after an incident where the pair clashed in practice, saying: “I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this.” Continue reading...

title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open with knee injury
summary: Two-time champion faces four months out after surgery World No 2 last played in July at Wimbledon Organisers have confirmed that two-time Australian Open champion Jannik Sinner has been ruled out of the grand slam at Melbourne Park ⁠in January after surgery on a persistent knee injury. Sinner said ⁠on Tuesday that ⁠he had ​had a minor operation, with Italian sports daily Corriere dello Sport reporting he was facing up to four months ⁠out, extending his long absence from the tour. Continue reading...

title: Two teams face Nations Championship relegation under 2030 playoff plans
summary: Bottom sides could face top Nations Cup sides from 2030 Tier-one teams expected to push back against plans Two teams could be relegated from the Nations Championship from 2030 under controversial plans being developed by the tournament organisers. The Guardian has learned that the favoured mechanism for introducing relegation is for the bottom sides in the northern and southern hemisphere tables to face a one-legged playoff match against the winners of the equivalent tables in the tier-two Nations Cup, which is run by World Rugby. The tier one sides would be guaranteed home advantage in the tie, which based on this year’s inaugural competition would see matches between Italy and Georgia and Fiji and the USA, with the winner of each securing a place in the Nations Championship two years later. Continue reading...

title: Woolly hats, battered bodies and big TV numbers mark rugby union’s new festival finale
summary: Nations Championship finals weekend can cement concept for future as players and coaches enjoy chance to let loose It would be a stretch to describe the Nations Championship finals weekend as the “Glastonbury of Rugby” quite yet. Cher will certainly need to wrap up warm if she is planning to make a cameo appearance; with forecast temperatures of 3C, plenty more thermal vests and woolly hats will be in evidence than at Worthy Farm in June. There will also be significant gaps in the Allianz Stadium moshpit when Italy and Fiji and Ireland and Australia kick off the three-day finals extravaganza beneath the Friday night lights. Even the organisers concede that Friday has been “a challenge” in terms of ticket sales and that’s without factoring in rush-hour traffic and public transport disruption. Continue reading...

title: Caleb Williams throws for game-winning TD as Bears stun Lions on Thanksgiving
summary: Chicago Bears 39-35 Detroit Lions QB throws TD pass to Odunze with three seconds left Detroit’s win streak ends at six games Caleb Williams threw a go-ahead six-yard touchdown pass to Rome Odunze with three seconds left to give the Chicago Bears their first lead of the game in a 39-35 win over the host Detroit Lions on Thursday to break a first-place tie in the NFC North. The Bears (9-2) have won six straight. Williams led the way, completing 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards with two touchdown passes after trailing by 11 points midway through the fourth quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs’s 70-yard run for his third score of the game. Continue reading...

title: Steelers owner backs Mike McCarthy and attacks Aaron Rodgers’s ‘insubordination’
summary: Art Rooney II has ‘100% confidence’ in head coach Insists QB’s outbursts could not be tolerated The Pittsburgh Steelers owner and president, Art Rooney II, has provided his full support to head coach, Mike McCarthy, in his stunning fallout with Aaron Rodgers, and described the quarterback’s actions as “insubordination”. Rodgers was ⁠benched on Tuesday night and waived the following day after he accused McCarthy of falling asleep during a meeting in an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show. Rodgers said McCarthy missed meetings and a ⁠walkthrough later that same week – ⁠claims that were corroborated ​by unnamed sources in a report by ESPN on Wednesday. The Steelers are preparing to face the Denver Broncos on Friday with Mason ⁠Rudolph at quarterback. Continue reading...

title: Super League returnees London Broncos eye new venues and Australia-friendly KO times
summary: Games possible on Thursdays and Saturday lunchtimes Double-header with Brisbane Broncos also mooted London Broncos are targeting Super League fixtures in new territories and new Australia-friendly kick-off times after returning to the top flight as part of their plan to grow rugby league, before campaigning to the NRL to be part of a unique double-header at Wembley in 2028 too. London will have a Super League presence in 2027 after the Rugby Football League awarded the Broncos the 15th place in a newly expanded competition. They swept aside all competition in the Championship last year, losing just one league fixture and winning a domestic treble with a squad many believed was Super League-ready. Continue reading...

title: Banton’s ascent to England leadership role vindicates all-in approach to white-ball game
summary: Batter assumes vice-captaincy and is set to step in as skipper in Canberra, with appointment a potential pointer to side’s future limited-overs direction When Will Jacks broke his hand at the MCG last Saturday night – his birthday ruined and his tour of Australia over – there were a few directions England could have turned as regards the vice-captaincy. Plenty of teams happily do without an official deputy, of course. But with Harry Brook jetting off to join the Test tour of South Africa after the fourth of these five T20 internationals, a replacement will be required when the series wraps up in Canberra. Phil Salt was one option. For all of his unfettered aggression, powered by those tattooed, Popeye-like forearms, the opener is an intelligent, thoughtful cricketer very much in tune with the rhythms of T20. As well as two seasons captaining in the Hundred, most recently with Welsh Fire, Salt previously deputised for Jos Buttler against Australia at home two years ago. Continue reading...

title: United States lined up to co-host 2034 men’s T20 World Cup with West Indies
summary: World body eager to build on 2028 Los Angeles Olympics England and Wales Cricket Board has ruled out a bid The United States is being lined up to co-host the 2034 men’s T20 World Cup in a joint enterprise with West Indies. The International Cricket Council announced the dates of all global events until 2035 after their quarterly meeting in Bali last week, but has not confirmed any venues beyond the 50-over World Cup in 2031 in India and Bangladesh. title: ‘Just taking part was a victory’: veterans’ sport helps recovery in Ukraine
summary: Photographer David Levene meets service personnel and veterans at selection trials in Lviv for next year’s Invictus Games in Birmingham It took a little longer than expected for the 100 or so archers to begin competing inside the large Soviet-era velodrome arena at MoD SKA in Lviv (built for the 1980 Moscow Olympics, it is Ukraine’s only indoor cycling track) on the first day of trials for the team that Ukraine will send to next year’s Invictus Games in Birmingham . The delay gave competitors a little extra time to stretch and practise. Coaches paraded up and down the line, giving some last-minute advice on strategy and technique to the waiting men and women facing down their targets. Pavlo and Vadym share a laugh during the laser tag trials. Pavlo lost his left leg from a landmine in 2023 and swimming became his path to physical and mental recovery. Vadym suffered a frontline injury in 2022. He set a Ukrainian record for runners with below-knee amputations, completing the 42km Marine Corps Marathon in 3hrs 30m in October 2026. Continue reading...

title: AFLW grand final: gap closes on three-peat chasing Kangaroos as Demons seek upset | Martin Pegan
summary: North Melbourne are out to secure their legacy but in their way stands a confident Melbourne side ready for their biggest test of the season The early chapters of the record books are still being written as the AFLW enters its second decade with North Melbourne now just one win away from a milestone that could stand the test of time. The Kangaroos have become the league’s benchmark during a dominant three seasons, and last year raised the bar higher as the first club to claim back-to-back premierships. A third consecutive grand final triumph when they face Melbourne at a sold out Ikon Park on Friday night would earn the Roos a larger slice of history – and cement their place as the competition’s first dynasty. The North Melbourne juggernaut has raised the standard of the AFLW; the Roos have lost only once since being defeated by Brisbane in the 2023 grand final, then turned the tables on the same rivals to win in the past two deciders. They romped through another campaign to finish the league’s 11th season as minor premiers with 11 victories and a percentage of 246.6%, though their record-breaking winning streak ended at 32 matches with a surprise loss to Hawthorn. Continue reading...
